steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Pulse walnuts in the bowl of a food processor until ground into a flour; transfer to a bowl. Stir in oats, flax meal, whole wheat flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt until thoroughly combined.

Combine almond butter, brown sugar, canola oil, agave nectar, egg, and vanilla extract in the bowl of a food processor; pulse to blend well. Transfer almond butter mixture to a large bowl; fold in chocolate chips and dried cherries. Stir oatmeal mixture into almond butter mixture; dough will be very thick.
Scoop dough by heaping teaspoons; roll into balls and place on the prepared baking sheets, about 2 inches apart.

Bake in the preheated oven until lightly browned, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove from the oven; flatten cookies with a spatula. Cool on the baking sheets for about 5 minutes before transferring to wire racks to finish cooling.

raw_recipe.headline: Whole Grain Breakfast Cookies Recipe
raw_recipe.description: This whole grain breakfast cookie recipe is made with oats, flax meal, and whole wheat flour, walnuts, almond butter, dried cherries, and chocolate chips.

review.reviewBody: I had to make a few substitutions, but these are just awesome. I used honey instead of agave nectar, applesauce instead of oil, and peanut butter instead of almond butter. I'm sure they would be even better with no substitutions, but this was a winner with my husband and my 17 month old!

Hearty and satisfying snack for any time of the day. Doubled recipe and made in half pan instead of cookies. Use 350 degrees instead of 375 degrees, but baked much longer because of thickness, at least 35-45 minutes, leaving residual heat to finish up.
Used sliced almonds because of walnut allergy, used three eggs instead of two, used whole flax seeds, added some ground wheat bran, dried cranberries instead of cherries. Did not add semi-sweet chocolate chips.
Came out great! We are nibbling on this and don't think it will last long!

I'm rating this recipe before actually making it because I have a question. I have all the ingredients except cherries and will use cranberries instead. My question: I love the texture of nuts and would like to use them finely chopped. If I do that it will change the amount of flour needed (I think). I could add ore flour or some protein powder or even some collagen peptides. Any idea how much more flour-y type stuff would be needed? I do love my breakfast cookies and I want to try these without ruining them by experimenting. Not the bravest of cooks.

I just made these today. I love cookies for breakfast (healthy). I decided to try making the walnut flour using my Nutribullet. I seem to have made walnut butter instead. Used it anyway. My agave was very old so I tossed it and used coconut sugar plus a tablespoon of water. I might try applesauce instead of oil next time. I also used craisins because I had them. That was the only thing I didn't have on hand. I used a cookie scoop, got nearly 30 cookies and I flattened them before baking. Good cookie.

I’ve made these a few times and have passed the recipe on to enthusiastic friends. I do have some changes: 1/3 cup melted margarine instead of canola oil; gluten-free flour and gluten-free oats; natural peanut butter instead of almond butter; 1/2 cup coconut instead of dried cherries; bring the chocolate chips down to 1/2 cup; local honey instead of agave; 2 eggs. The mix is extremely sticky and difficult to work with so I refrigerate for 20 minutes before spooning onto the cookie sheets - this makes all the difference in the world! I also flatten the cookies before baking, with the bottom of a tumbler dipped in sugar or flour. This is a labour intensive recipe but so so good!

Adults and four children all enjoyed this for breakfast. I followed the cook’s suggested sub of extra brown sugar, but used just two extra tablespoons plus two of honey. I used almond flour instead of walnut flour, and half/half almond butter/peanut butter. The dough was crumbly enough to take a whole extra egg rather than the one suggested white. Still five stars because the recipe works even you don’t have exact ingredients on hand. It is self evident if you need to add extra moisture at the end to make it hold together, depending on how wet your sweetener is. Made 30 disher #40 (1 1/2 Tbs.) cookies for me. Hefty eaters ate three apiece.

These are BY FAR the best ‘healthier’ Cookies I have ever made. I just used almond flour instead of grinding the walnuts and I mixed all my wet ingredients (sans the egg) and microwaved for a few seconds to melt the butter, coconut oil(subbed for oil), honey (out of agave), & peanut butter (subbed for almond butter) for ease of mixing, then added the egg and worked it into the dry ingredients. I used half dates & half dried cherries and soaked them in a bit of hot water before adding them & the chocolate chips. 
I do agree that they might benefit from an extra egg because they are a bit crumbly... but YUMMY!!!

So easy and SO delicious! My very picky sons love them and these are the only cookies we keep in the house now. I did make some adjustments. I used candies pecans instead of walnuts, added 1/3 cup of coconut flakes and omitted the cherries. I also used about 2/3 cup peanut butter (instead of almond butter) which helped them hold together better. I cooked them at 350 because 375 at 9 minutes burned them the first time. I will definitely be making these a lot for kids school lunches!

Thank you so much for sharing this healthy & very delicious cookie recipe.
I changed it a bit using the ingredients on hand.
peaunt butter > almond butter
1/2 cup sugar > syrup + sugar
2 eggs > 1 egg
coconut oil > canola oil
dates, processed with the wet ingredients > dried cherries
Finally baked at 350F for 12mins because I love crispy cookie.
The aroma was so nice even before baking. I couldn't stop eating but didn't feel guilty because all are healthy ingredients. Yummy!!
I'll make it again & again.

I would say. For texture you have to pulse the oatmeal and dry ingredience... since you are usinig whole oatmeal not quick. I like everything about this recipe much healthier than most recipes, and you can easily swap out things you might not have on hand, for example peanut butter for almond brown sugar or honey for agave etc. I was curious how much does 1 cup of walnuts process into when you pulse it into flour? anyone?? I had almond flour on hand so I used that.

We love these! We added 2 eggs instead of one, half cup almond flour instead of walnuts(didn't have), peanut butter for almond, and the brown sugar sub instead of agave. They are really good. It's hard to find a good breakfast cookie that doesn't have banana! These are winners with my SUPER picky daughter and the whole family. Just made a second batch tonight!

Substituted the Almond butter with pumpkin and it turned out great. added the extra egg and cut down on the brown sugar. Used applesauce instead of oil. went with Dark chocolate chips. 
All together - great snack...I love the base of this recipe because you can mix it up with whatever you want. I made bars. It gets sticky but just wet hands with water when you shape them and pressed with a spatula to about 3/8 of and inch. 10 to 12 min. 
I will make again. Thanks

Made these for my grandsons to have before school. They all gave the recipe two thumbs up! I had to substitute craisins since my store didn't have dried cherries, and I used almond flour instead of grinding the walnuts. I'm sure they would be terrific either way. I had trouble incorporating all the chocolate chips so i will try with 3/4 cup next time. The only problem is that they get eaten so fast!

These are very satisfying and tasty. I used peanut butter instead of almond butter because that’s what I had. And I used dried cranberries instead of cherries because I had those on hand as well. I also added a teaspoon of cardamom. If they’re not allowed to cool enough in the pan they are very crumbly; however, I discovered that they held together better by letting them cool longer in the pan before putting them on a wire rack. One person suggested using two eggs instead of one, and I will try that next time.

I used almond flour for the walnuts, left out the cinnamon, maple syrup for the agave, added an extra egg and left out the cherries. Biggest change was I used sunbutter so my grandchild could take to school where nuts butters are not allowed. Warning: the inside will be bright GREEN! The sunbutter reacts to the baking soda and causes a chemical reaction that turns the inside of the cookie bright green! Perfectly safe and doesn’t affect the taste. My grandson thought they looked cool and called them monster cookies! You can easily get a full cup of the chocolate chips in the batter if you follow the directions and stir them into the liquid ingredients first and use MINI chips. I didn’t need to roll into balls, just scooped and they flatten on their own like a regular cookie, no need to flatten after baking. Good taste, soft and green inside😉

I use raisins instead of dried cherries and omit the chocolate chips. This cookie is a staple at our house and whenever our 50 y.o. son visits I have to have a batch at the ready plus extras for him to take home.
So yummy with morning coffee! Made exactly as recipe states.

I don’t know how but my walnuts turned into walnut butter instead of walnut flour. Not sure why that happened but I followed the rest of the recipe substituting only honey for agave and peanut butter for almond butter. I don’t think those substitutions would have changed the recipe so drastically. There is not enough flour (or flour substitutes or oats) in this recipe. There is also too many add-ins with a full cup of chocolate chips and half cup of cherries. I ended up with a lot of chocolate chips at the bottom of the mixing bowl. These cookies didn’t hit for me. Maybe using almond flour or store bought walnut flour would help, but I still think the chocolate chips need to be reduced. The cookies were an odd texture like flax energy balls or something. I know I won’t be able to sell these as a cookie to my 4 year old which is why I made them.

I just really need suggestions (I have not made this yet but this site requires a star !)! I have read most/all? reviews. I have a child with nut allergies (that incls. coconut) and one that has to be gluten free. I see many gluten free sub ideas = what can be subbed for PB or Almond Butter? Can Anyone help me ?

A nice cookie that is healthful enough to justify as a breakfast but satisfying enough as a treat. Based on other reviews, I used two eggs and added three tablespoons of dry milk powder for a little bonus nutrition. We left out dried cherries, honey instead of agave, peanut butter instead of almond butter, and cut the chocolate chips down to 10 tablespoons (based on what we had). Cookies were plenty sweet for all our tastes (including our 6 yo). Chocolate chips were hard to roll without having them fall out, as previous folks have mentioned. I might try to use chocolate chunks instead next time to see if it’s easier.
